source: Both takes were written by hand against the composer system prompt in grounds/compose.py, because no API key was available when this was built. They are stand-ins, not transcripts of a real model response. Replace them with genuine recorded output once a key is set: run with --live and save the raw text here. Either way they go through the same verification path a live call does, which is the point of keeping them.

takes.label: accepted
takes.comment: Uses only figures present in the input. Passes the number guard.

takes.label: rejected
takes.comment: Deliberately bad. Invents a total, invents a share of revenue, invents a peer benchmark, and adds sales language. The number guard catches it and the brief falls back to the deterministic opening. This take exists so the guard can be watched working without a network call.
